  Defense: Basic. Never blocks wins (R1). Random setups include a Magpie only if at least a third of the roles have tokens.
  Night: may steal a token from another player (a visit). It happens at the end of the night, after that night's
  token use, so a token used tonight can't be stolen. The stolen token is gone (you can't use it). You are told
  whether you stole one, not its kind; they are told which kind they lost. If they have no tokens, nothing
  happens and they aren't told. A steal from a player who dies that night still takes the token and counts (R10).
  Win: iff you steal tokens from 3 different players (a second steal from the same player takes nothing). If you
  are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game (as for the Executioner). If you died
  that night, you still win and nothing is revealed.

Vulture
  Win: alone, if you are alive at the start of a Day (after the night's deaths) and your threshold or fewer players
  are alive, counting yourself. The game then ends at once and everyone else loses (wins already earned by roles
  that never block wins still count, R1). Your threshold starts at 2.
  Night: may visit another player. If they die that night (by any cause, end-of-night effects included), you are
  told at the end of the night that they died and their role (exact-role check, R19; nothing more if a Mortician
  cleaned them), and you get the first of these power-ups you don't have yet: +1 to your threshold, Standard
  Defense, +1 to your threshold, Strong Defense, then +1 to your threshold for each later one. Your threshold
  never goes above max(floor(N/3), 2), where N is the number of players at the start of the game; a power-up that
  would raise it further is skipped. If they don't die, nothing happens and you are told so.

Decoy
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you die at night. You lose if you die by Day or the game ends with you alive.
  If an attack killed you at night, the next Day's announcements say you were the Decoy and name 3 players: every
  player whose attack would have killed you on its own (3 of them at random if there were more), then random other
  players alive at the start of that Day to make 3 (fewer if not enough are left). The names are in random order,
  and the announcement doesn't say how many of them attacked you. Your cause of death and last will show as usual.

=== PART 7: TRAITS ===

R24 (Traits)
Some players also have a trait: an extra ability on top of their role. You are told your own trait at the start
(except a hidden trait, which says so); nobody else is told, not even your teammates, and whether a game has any
traits is secret. Investigations never see traits: they report roles and alignments only. A trait stays with you if
your role changes. Traits are always true: a Roleplayer's trait is real even though its role isn't. A player may
have more than one trait, but never the same one twice. Each trait below says who can get it (Who), whether it is
hidden from its holder (Hidden), whether at most one player in a game has it (Unique), what it does (Effect) and
which traits nobody holds together with it (Never with). A trait's night action is used in addition to your role's
own, and a role-block stops it too.

--- Village players only ---

Martyr
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the announcement of your death also says you were a Martyr and names every player whose
  vote counted as Guilty in your trial. Your role stays hidden. A Martyr who dies any other way shows nothing.

Cursed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you die, a random living Good player (if any) is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night: the
  night you died, or the night after the Day you died. It comes after all of that night's other actions and attacks,
  so the victim is drawn from the Good players still alive then, and it counts as a death that night. Its cause is
  "a curse". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Avenger
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are killed at night, every player whose attack would have killed you is dealt a Basic Attack (an
  Astral Visit) that same night. Defense and protection apply as usual (R3); a kill's cause is "Avenger". Attacks
  that weren't fatal on their own, and deaths by Day, set nothing off. It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't
  stop it.

Kindred
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn up to two random other players whose votes counted the
  same way as the vote you cast (if fewer did, you learn that). It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Remorseful
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Guilty in a trial and that player is hanged and was Village (their true alignment), you die at
  once; the cause is "remorse". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks
  counts it.
  Never with: Zealot.

Ashamed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Innocent in a trial and that player is hanged and wasn't Village (their true alignment: Yakuza
  or Neutral), you die at once; the cause is "shame". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing
  that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Merciful or Turncoat.

Faultline
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn one random other player whose vote counted as Guilty
  and one whose vote counted as Innocent (if all the others voted one way, you learn that). It needs no action, so a
  role-block doesn't stop it.

Notorious
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19). Checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count,
  aren't fooled.
  Never with: Turncoat.

Stolen Blade
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may attack another living player with a stolen Katana: a Standard Attack,
  besides your role's own action. It is an action and a visit by you, and it looks exactly like the Yakuza's Katana
  attack: a kill's cause is "Katana", and a surviving target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana.
  You learn only whether it killed. A role-block stops it, and then it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed.

Paranoid
  Who: Village players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/4, you are told you were attacked and survived, though nobody attacked
  you. The made-up attack is the Katana's 2/3 of the time, and otherwise a Vigilante's or a Serial Killer's (always
  the Katana's when neither role can be in the game); it is worded like a real one. Nothing else happens: it isn't a
  visit or an attack, and nobody else learns of it.
  Never with: Oblivious.

Turncoat
  Who: Village players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise, even if the Village wins.
  Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19); checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count, see you
  as Good. You stay Village in every other way: you aren't in the Yakuza's chat or Katana votes, you don't know who
  the Yakuza are, and they aren't told about you. The game's end ignores you, like a role that never blocks wins
  (R1): it ends when the other living players are all Village or all Yakuza.
  Never with: Ashamed, Notorious, Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Spiteful.

Spiteful
  Who: Village players only, except a Saint.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: If you are hanged, from then on you win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise,
  even if the Village wins. Until then you win with the Village as usual, and dying any other way changes nothing.
  Nobody is told you switched, and your will is revealed as usual.
  Never with: Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Turncoat.

--- Yakuza players only ---

Spare Blade
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may make one extra Katana attack on another living player, whoever holds the
  Katana and besides its own attack (which the Yakuza still choose as usual, R8). It is Standard, an action and a
  visit by you, and its target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana. A role-block stops it, and then
  it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed or Berserker.

Usurper
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win while you are the only Yakuza alive, and then you take the win alone: the
  other Yakuza, alive or dead, don't win. If the Yakuza win with another Yakuza alive, they win and you don't. Your
  teammates aren't told.
  Never with: Selfish or Selfless.

Shaky
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Every Katana attack you make (the Katana's own while you hold it, or a Spare Blade attack) is level None,
  so it never kills (R3); it is still an attack and a visit.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Katana Master.

Katana Expert
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its own attack Strong instead of Standard.
  Choose it with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at
  the end of that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along
  with the attack, and it isn't used up.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Master or Shaky.

Katana Master
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Like Katana Expert, but the attack is Divine, which no Defense, protection, trap or charm stops.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Shaky.

Berserker
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its attack rampage: besides its own attack, it
  makes a Standard Katana attack on every other player who visits its target that night, whatever their faction.
  These attacks on visitors aren't visits, and Astral Visits aren't visits, so their makers aren't attacked. Choose it
  with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at the end of
  that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along with the
  attack, and it isn't used up. Each attacked player learns only that they were attacked with the Katana; you learn
  how many players the rampage attacked and how many of those attacks killed, not who the visitors were.
  Never with: Katana Expert, Katana Master, Shaky or Spare Blade.

--- Village and Yakuza players only ---

Armed
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may fire a hidden gun at another living player: a Basic Attack. It is an
  action and a visit, and a role-blocked shot isn't used up. You learn only whether it killed its target. A kill's
  cause is "a hidden gun".
  Never with: Spare Blade or Stolen Blade.

Bonded
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random Village or Yakuza player are bonded, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role or faction). If either of you dies, the other dies of heartbreak at once (its cause is
  "heartbreak"). Heartbreak isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Rival.

Rival
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random player of your own faction are rivals, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role). Each of you wins only if your faction wins and the other has died by the end; whether you are
  alive doesn't matter. Your faction's win doesn't change.
  Never with: Bonded, Spiteful or Turncoat.

Selfish
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are alive at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you
  just don't share it if you died.
  Never with: Selfless, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

Selfless
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are dead at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you just
  don't share it if you're alive.
  Never with: Selfish, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

--- Any player ---

Grudge
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the next night one random player whose vote counted as Guilty in your trial, among
  those alive when that night begins, is dealt a Standard Attack (an Astral Visit). Defense and protection apply as
  usual. A kill's cause is "a grudge". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Loud
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You earn 1.5 times the usual speaking budget each round, and your cap is 1.5 times the usual (R22). Your
  prices and trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Curt
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: The length part of your message prices (R22) is doubled, so long messages cost you much more; each
  message's base fee, nominations and your trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Confidant
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Once per game, on one of your own Day turns, you may send one private message hidden: nobody else is told
  it was sent, and the public ledger doesn't count it. Its recipient sees that it was hidden. Players who hear
  private messages (e.g. the Wiretap) still hear it, also marked hidden.

Zealot
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Every Guilty/Innocent trial vote you cast counts as Guilty, whatever you vote, including in your own
  trial. Your nomination (Yes/No) votes are unchanged. Your private reminder shows both the vote you cast and how it
  counted, and everything that reports how you voted (e.g. the Auditor, a Martyr's announcement) uses the vote as
  counted. A Fixer's reversal doesn't change it.
  Never with: Merciful or Remorseful.

Merciful
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Like Zealot, but your trial votes always count as Innocent.
  Never with: Ashamed or Zealot.

Drowsy
  Who: Any player whose role has a night action and can be role-blocked.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/2, you are role-blocked (R9) with no blocker. On those nights you are
  told you were role-blocked, as with any role-block.

Stocked
  Who: Any player whose role starts with tokens and can ever have more than it starts with.
  Effect: You start with one more of each kind of token your role starts with.

Disguised
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You are told a Village role (never your own), drawn at the start. Every exact-role check (R18) sees you as
  that role instead of yours, alive or dead; alignment checks still see your true alignment.

Narrow Escape
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Once per game, on the first night an attack that isn't Divine would kill you (after Defense, protection,
  traps and charms), you survive: every non-Divine attack on you that night fails instead. It works like Strong
  Defense on every night until then, so a night when nothing would have killed you (e.g. a Medic stopped the attack)
  doesn't use it up. Divine Attacks and deaths by Day aren't stopped. You are told about the failed attacks as for
  any others (R3).

Oblivious
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: You are never told about an attack you survive.
  Never with: Paranoid.

Sleepwalker
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Every night you visit one random other living player, besides any action of your own; code draws it, and
  you aren't told whom. It does nothing but visit: anything that sees or reacts to visits (R6), such as a Tracker, a
  Lookout or a Veteran's alert, counts it. It isn't optional, but a role-block stops it (R7).

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Diviner who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the divine op; code draws the role and tells them. Don't tell() the Diviner anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. If they picked a Yakuza, don't use the op: that player has Strong Defense tonight, and the Diviner gets no result.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks, unless it was role-blocked (R9; set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder, a Kitsune's release for the Kitsune; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- A Hitman's attack is a Basic Attack: pass by=<the Hitman> on the kill op, since code counts its kills from the killers. Code tells it whether a kill counted and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about that.
- An Insomniac who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the stay_awake op, which spends the token; code tells them the roles of up to 3 random players from your record_visits list. Don't tell() the Insomniac anything about it. Staying awake is not a visit: don't put it in record_visits.
- Kitsune: a Kitsune with no swallowed attack who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) laid a fox charm on its target. Resolve the charm FIRST, before any other protection (Medic, Trapper, ...): use the kitsune_charm op with every non-Divine Attack on the charmed player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert, an Enforcer's attack or a trap's hit-back), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced, e.g. 'Katana', 'Serial Killer')}, [] if none. Code picks the one the charm swallows and says which: treat it as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), then resolve the other attacks normally. Several charms on one player: one kitsune_charm op each, every one listing all the attacks; code has them act in random order, each swallowing a different attack. A Kitsune holding a swallowed attack can't charm; if it acted with a target (and wasn't role-blocked), use the kitsune_release op: code says the attack's level and cause, and you resolve it like any attack by the Kitsune on that target (a visit). If it kills, kill with exactly that cause, by the Kitsune, katana false; a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Kitsune. Code tells the Kitsune its results; don't tell() it about the charm or the release.
- Mirror Maker: a Mirror Maker who acted on another player (and wasn't role-blocked) placed a mirror on them (it spends a token). Resolve it right after any fox charm (Kitsune) and before traps and Defense: use the mirror op with every non-Divine Attack on the mirrored player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert or an Enforcer's attack), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}, [] if none. Don't list the attacks code reflects (below). Code says which attacks the mirror stops (all of them, except one a fox charm already swallowed): treat each as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), so traps and Medics on that player have nothing left to stop. For each stopped visit, code says it is reflected: resolve it as an Attack of the same level on its attacker (an Astral Visit, never reflected again: a mirror on the attacker just stops it), against their Defense, protection, traps and charms as usual. If it kills, kill with exactly the stopped attack's cause, by the Mirror Maker, katana false (a reflected Katana attack reads as a Katana death); a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Mirror Maker. Several mirrors on one player: one op each, every one listing all the attacks; they stop the attacks together. Code tells the Mirror Maker its result; don't tell() it.
- Oathsworn: an Oathsworn who spent its token (and wasn't role-blocked) marks its target: use the swear op, which spends the token; it is a visit to the target only, and nothing else happens that night (nobody is told). On the next Night, if the Oathsworn is dead when the Night begins, code says so in tonight's notes: call record_visits first, then the fulfil_oath op ({op:'fulfil_oath', by: <the dead Oathsworn>}): code lists the Divine Attacks, cause 'a blood oath', on the marked player and on every other player who visited them tonight (Astral Visits, not visits; Astral visitors aren't hit). Divine Attacks beat every Defense and ignore protection, traps, charms, mirrors and Narrow Escape, so each one kills.
- Trapper: traps persist across nights and code keeps them. For each Trapper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked), use the set_trap op before any spring_trap: player = where its trap goes, or null if it acted with no target (that removes its trap). A new trap replaces its old one at once, so the old one doesn't act tonight. Trapping the player its trap is already on isn't allowed (the trap stays): code refuses it. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed (trapped_by status lists the traps on a player). If anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a player with an armed trap tonight, use the spring_trap op once for that player with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code has every armed trap on that player act in random order, each stopping a different attack, and uses them up: treat each stopped attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether each trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trappers their results; don't tell() them about traps.
- Veteran on alert (spent an alert token; set_tokens): Standard Defense, can't be role-blocked, and a Strong Attack on every player who visited them tonight, of any faction, including a role-blocker and the Katana holder if it attacked them. Astral Visits aren't hit. Not a visit. Tell the Veteran whether anyone visited and, if so, how many and whether each attack succeeded (e.g. '2 players visited you: your attack killed one and failed on the other'), never who they were.
- Werewolf: on even-numbered Nights only, a Werewolf who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) rampages: at its target's house (a visit to them; put it in record_visits) or, with no target or itself as target, at home (not a visit). Call record_visits first, then the rampage op ({op:'rampage', by, player}, player left out for a home rampage): code lists the Strong Attacks it deals, cause 'Werewolf', from the recorded visits: on the target (a visit) and on every other player who visited the target (or, at home, the Werewolf) tonight, of any faction (not visits; Astral Visits aren't visits, so they aren't hit). Resolve each like any attack (Defense, Medics, charms, traps, mirrors: give the visit flag code gives). An Enforcer counts a rampage at a player's house, its hits on visitors included, as an Attack of the Werewolf's own choosing; a home rampage doesn't count. Tell the Werewolf how many players it attacked and how many of those attacks killed, never who the visitors were (e.g. 'Your rampage attacked 3 players and killed 2').
- Cursed (a trait, R24): for a Cursed player who died today or dies tonight, code deals a Divine Attack on a random Good player after your resolution, at the end of the night. Don't draw or kill a victim yourself.
- Notorious (a trait; see each player's traits): every alignment check reads a Notorious player as Evil (Sheriff: Evil; Seer: Evil), like a framed player (R19). The Census Taker's count still sees their true alignment. Don't tell anyone a player is Notorious.
- Spare Blade (a trait, R24): a Yakuza whose trait_actions has trait 'Spare Blade' makes one extra Katana attack on its target, besides the Katana's own attack and whoever holds the Katana: Standard (R8), an action and a visit by them (record it), and it counts as an attack everywhere one does. A role-block stops it, and then it isn't used. Unless they were role-blocked, use the spare_blade op (it marks it used, even if the attack fails) and resolve the attack: a kill's cause is 'Katana', katana=true, by the user; a survivor is told they were attacked with the Katana, as for the Katana's own attack. Tell the user only whether it killed. Never mention the trait to anyone else.
- Stolen Blade (a trait, R24): a Village player whose trait_actions has trait 'Stolen Blade' makes one Standard Attack on its target, besides their role's action: an action and a visit by them (record it), and it counts as an attack everywhere one does. A role-block stops it, and then it isn't used. Unless they were role-blocked, use the stolen_blade op (it marks it used, even if the attack fails) and resolve the attack: a kill's cause is 'Katana' (katana=false, by the user); a survivor is told they were attacked with the Katana, exactly as for the Yakuza's. Tell the user only whether it killed. Never mention the trait to anyone else, and the Yakuza aren't told who made it.
- Bonded (a trait, R24): Dave and Niaj. When one of a pair dies, code kills the other at once (cause heartbreak, not an attack). Never kill anyone for heartbreak yourself.
- Oblivious (a hidden trait, R24): never tell Mallory about an attack they survive tonight (code tells a death as usual). Everything else about the attack is unchanged: protectors still learn they stopped it, the attacker still learns it failed. Never mention the trait.
